name: Tiroler Volkskunstmuseum
kurzbeschreibung: The Tyrolean Folk Art Museum in Innsbruck exhibits historic wood-paneled parlors, traditional costumes, carnival masks, and nativity crèches.
beschreibung:
Overview

The acclaimed Tyrolean Folk Art Museum (Tiroler Volkskunstmuseum) on Universitätsstraße in Innsbruck is celebrated internationally as one of the most comprehensive and evocative regional culture museums in the entire European Alpine realm. Housed within the venerable wings of a Renaissance Franciscan monastery immediately adjoining the Imperial Hofburg and the Court Church (Hofkirche), the institution preserves the rich tangible and spiritual heritage of historic Tyrol. Its masterful permanent exhibition meticulously documents the domestic lifestyles, artisan craftsmanship, and deeply rooted folk customs of farming and bourgeois communities across the valleys of North, East, and South Tyrol spanning centuries.

Route & Requirements

A crowning highlight of the collection consists of more than a dozen authentic, wood-paneled historic parlors (Stuben) from the Gothic, Renaissance, and Baroque eras, transplanted piece by piece from alpine farmhouses and patrician homes to recreate genuine historical living environments. Additional fascinating exhibition sections display vibrant regional Tyrolean folk costumes, ornamental pewter and pottery, traditional farming implements, reverse glass paintings, and carved votive offerings. World-renowned is the expressive collection of alpine carnival masks, featuring fearsome wooden carvings of the Muller, Roller, and Scheller traditions. The ground floor enchants with one of Central Europe's finest collections of historic nativity scenes carved from wood and wax, illuminated by multilingual multimedia guides.

Visit & Arrival

The museum welcomes visitors year-round daily from 09:00 to 17:00. The standard adult ticket costs approx. €12.00 and includes direct admission into the adjoining Court Church with Emperor Maximilian I's tomb monument; children and youth under 19 enjoy free admission (fully included with the Innsbruck Card). Multilingual audio guides provide insightful narrative commentary on the folk art treasures. Arrival: centrally located in the old town, a ten-minute walk from Innsbruck Hauptbahnhof. Tram routes 1 and 3 stop at the Museumstraße station; drivers can utilize the nearby Congress underground garage.

Tips

Begin your visit with the captivating multimedia presentation in the former Chapter Hall, which provides an engaging historical foundation on Emperor Maximilian I's empire. All museum levels are equipped with modern elevators and ramps, providing full step-free accessibility for wheelchairs and strollers. Allow ample time to marvel at the famous bronze statues of the adjacent Court Church and explore traditional artisan shops and the nearby imperial Hofgarten gardens.
preis: Adults approx. €12.00 (combined ticket including Court Church), under 19 free (free with Innsbruck Card)
